body.objective: Make concurrent read-only `s-f` invocations safe. During the coordinator sweep, parallel `s-f work ready` and `s-f inbox` calls raced while rebuilding the shared `sfc` executable and repeatedly failed with `s-f: sfc build failed`; an immediate serialized direct compiler invocation succeeded. This prevents the coordinator from querying independent streams concurrently and turns a read-only status operation into an intermittent substrate failure.
body.stop_condition: Add a process-safe launcher build/cache protocol: derive the cache key from the complete compiler, sfc source and include-path inputs; serialize one build per key with an OS-level lock or build to a unique temporary path and atomically publish only a verified executable; let concurrent callers wait for or reuse the completed artifact; preserve the last known-good executable if a rebuild fails; and return the actual compiler stderr for a genuine failure. Add a deterministic stress test launching at least twelve mixed `s-f work ready`, `s-f inbox`, `s-f work show` and `s-f overview` processes against one programme while forcing a cache miss. Every process must either succeed against one content-addressed executable or report the same genuine compile error, with no partial binary, truncated output, shared-temp collision or false build-failed result.
body.forbid: no global deletion of the cached executable before a replacement is verified; no fixed shared temporary output path without locking; no silent fallback to an executable whose content key does not match current inputs; no swallowing compiler diagnostics; no serialization of the actual read-only programme queries after the build is ready; no work-item transition, lease, git or terminal-title mutation
notes: Minimal live reproduction from the physics programme on 2026-07-20: launch three shells concurrently, each running one or more `s-f work ready --stream <stream> --now 2026-07-20T14:53:00Z` or `s-f inbox --stream <stream>` commands after an sfc source change. Multiple callers returned exit 3 with `sfc build failed`; `/home/alstrup/.local/bin/forge -I /home/alstrup/area9/tango/forge/tools/datalog -I /home/alstrup/area9/tango/forge/tools/science-forge/conflux /home/alstrup/area9/tango/forge/tools/science-forge/sfc.forge` then compiled successfully when run alone.
First consumer is the recurring multi-stream coordinator sweep. Serialized calls work but unnecessarily multiply the already high dashboard/query latency.
The stress fixture should exercise both a successful rebuild and an intentionally invalid source so the launcher distinguishes a real compiler failure from a publication race.
